pr_title: fix(rust,python): fix `csv` parser error when commented-out rows precede the header row
pr_body:
Closes #13022.

The linked issue mentions `raise_if_empty` but that's a red herring; the real issue is that we were trying to skip the header row _before_ we had skipped the pre-header rows (including comments), instead of after. Reordering those two operations so that the correct lines are skipped solves the error.

Added some additional comment/skip permutations to the existing test coverage.

Also: the slightly misleadingly-named `skip_header` function didn't actually have any header-specific logic; was just a simple redirect to `skip_this_line`, so we may as well just call that directly.

issue_context.title: parameter `raise_if_empty` doesn't work with `comment_prefix` in `read_csv` gives `polars.exceptions.NoDataError: not enough lines to skip`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

minimal example input file, `test.tsv`
```
##comment to skip
Col1    Col2
```
Python code:
```python
import polars as pl
df = pl.read_csv('test.tsv', separator = '\t', comment_prefix='##', raise_if_empty=False)
```


### Log output

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "<path>/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/utils/deprecation.py", line 100, in wrapper
    return function(*args, **kwargs)
  File "<path>/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/io/csv/functions.py", line 369, in read_csv
    df = pl.DataFrame._read_csv(
  File "<path>/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/dataframe/frame.py", line 775, in _read_csv
    self._df = PyDataFrame.read_csv(
polars.exceptions.NoDataError: not enough lines to skip
```


### Issue description

The given minimal file and example give error `polars.exceptions.NoDataError: not enough lines to skip`. Detailed log added. However, if there's a file with NoData (without data, just columns) and no comments, the same loads without an error. 

### Expected behavior

Expected behavior is to just load the columns as with files where comment prefix is not present. Expected output:
```
file < 128 rows, no statistics determined                                                                 
no. of chunks: 1 processed by: 1 threads.                                                                 
shape: (0, 2)
┌──────┬──────┐
│ Col1 ┆ Col2 │
│ ---  ┆ ---  │
│ str  ┆ str  │
╞══════╪══════╡
```

comments: Thanks for the clean example - will be fixed in the upcoming release. (Note that the value of `raise_if_empty` wasn't connected to the error, there was actually a slightly different issue with parser logic that has now been resolved) 👌
